parts.transcript: S2: Dave, manager of Creton (audio: Cretan) Running Sports Club, on the annual run. Start in front of the castle this year (11, park being refurbished). Distance lengthened to 7 miles (12, from 5). Prize: sports equipment worth ~1000 pounds for the winner (13). Finish line is on the ground of the station (14). Register at the town hall (15, no internet enrolment this year), free. Age limit: must be at least 16, so under 16 not allowed (16). Bring an extra pair of shoes and a jacket (17). Training advice for self-trainers: run with a friend/rival not in groups (B), make a record of your running time (F), get used to different roads and paths (G) (18-20=B,F,G). Warm-up is taught in the club's trainer-led class (not self-advice); 'all weather' rejected (held in good weather); 'dogs' is 'don't just jog with your dog'.

parts.title: Boar and Red Deer
parts.transcript: S4: lecture by Jim Robinson on wild boar and red deer. Boar is not a protected species (31, not on the protected animals list). Numbers should be controlled due to damage to the environment (32). They spread diseases that infect other species (33). Poison is banned by legislation for killing boars (34). Forest-dwelling boar should be kept in the forest away from people/cities (35). Early 1990s population rise as boar broke free/escaped from farms (36). Red deer also damage produce like grain and potatoes (37). As weather gets colder deer come to villages looking for food (38). Deer population should be kept stable for hunting traditions (39). Real concern: deer devastate farmers' crops (40).
